findings.title: Commit-plan block reuse ignoring collision mismatch is untested
findings.claim: The guard that forbids reusing a visually-identical pool block whose colind differs (classic-commit-plan.ts:371-374) is pinned by no test — deleting the colind check leaves all 24 classic-commit-plan tests green.
findings.evidence: PLANT: removed `if ((doc.collision.colind[b] ?? 0) !== colind) continue;` at classic-commit-plan.ts:374 → `npx vitest run src/core/art/__tests__/classic-commit-plan.test.ts` = 24/24 pass. planCanvasCommit is imported by exactly one test file (grep). Failure scenario: a 2C canvas commit whose region overlaps a look-alike block (same 4 tiles/flips/pals, different colind — decorative vs solid variants) reuses the wrong block id; chunk cells save cleanly and the disasm silently gets wrong collision, with no downstream defense — writeS1Level round-trips it fine. Measured S1 fact: one block can reach 55 chunks, so the blast radius is large.
findings.fix: Add a test: doc with two blocks identical in cells but colind 0 vs N; commit art matching that shape needing colind N (via displaced cell); assert the plan reuses ONLY the colind-matching block / mints a new block rather than reusing the colind-0 one.

verdict.reasoning:
I attempted to refute and could not; the coverage gap is real and I reproduced it end to end.

WHAT THE GUARD DOES. classic-commit-plan.ts:373-383, inside internBlock, scans doc.blocks ascending for a pool block whose 4 cells match the drawn def; line 374 skips any candidate whose doc.collision.colind[b] differs from the colind inherited from the displaced chunk cell (computed at line 413). This is a DIFFERENT mechanism from the intern-key dedup at line 367 (`...#${colind}`), which only separates blocks minted within this same commit. Line 374 is the only thing protecting reuse of a PRE-EXISTING pool block.

MUTATION SURVIVAL — VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY (repo untouched). I copied src/ + vitest.config.ts to scratchpad with node_modules symlinked, deleted line 374 there, and ran tests: baseline classic-commit-plan.test.ts = 24/24 pass; mutant = 24/24 pass. I then ran the ENTIRE suite against the mutant: 170 files passed / 1 skipped, 2293 tests passed / 1 skipped — byte-identical to baseline. So the guard is unpinned not just by the cited file but by the whole 2294-test suite. `git status --short -- src` afterwards: clean.

ONE SEAT DETAIL IS WRONG, BUT IT CUTS AGAINST THE SEAT. The evidence says "planCanvasCommit is imported by exactly one test file". False: it is imported by src/renderer/state/classicLevelStore.ts, src/renderer/components/canvas/canvas-commit-model.ts and CommitPlanView.tsx, and indirectly exercised by classicLevelStore.test.ts and canvas-commit-model.test.ts. Those suites still pass with the guard deleted, so the conclusion (zero coverage) survives the misstatement.

WHY THE EXISTING "LOOKS IDENTICAL BUT DIFFERENT COLLISION" TEST (test file :300) MISSES IT. That test paints canvasIndex(1,5), which resolves to a brand-new solid tile at pal:1, while pool blocks 1 and 3 hold tiles 1-4 at pal:0. The pool scan at :373 therefore never finds a visual match, so the assertion (two colind values in blockWrites) is satisfied purely by the intern key at :367. Deleting :374 leaves it green — which I confirmed.

BEHAVIORAL PROOF OF THE DEFECT THE GUARD PREVENTS. Concrete triggering state: doc with tile 5 = 0x55 (solid entry 5); block 1 = 4x{tile:5,pal:1} with colind 0; block 3 = identical cells with colind 7; chunk 0 = 256 cells of block 3. Commit a solid canvasIndex(1,5) canvas over target {chunkFileIndex: 0}. With the guard: chunkWrites[0] cells all reference block 3 (colind 7 preserved), blocksReused=1. Without the guard: cells all reference block 1 (colind 0) — the chunk silently loses its collision. Both runs return ok:true with no warning, so nothing downstream flags it.

THE SHAPE IS REAL IN S1, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Using Aurora's own enigmaDecompress on /home/volence/sonic_hacks/s1disasm/map16/*.eni cross-referenced with decodeS1ColInd over collide/*.bin, groups of byte-identical blocks carrying DIFFERENT colind: GHZ 5 groups, MZ 1 group (LZ, SLZ, SYZ, SBZ 0). Example GHZ: blocks 1 and 393 share cells 4054,4854,4854,4054 with colind 255 vs 251; blocks 325/396 (255 vs 252); 326/397 (255 vs 252); 329/395 (255 vs 253). Because the scan runs ascending from b=1, block 1 is the first hit for its shape, so the unguarded path would pick exactly the wrong variant.

The proposed fix is correct, with one addition: the fixture must make the pool block visually REACHABLE (a solid pool tile plus a matching pal line), which is exactly where the existing :300 test falls short.
verdict.severity_correction: Downgrade high -> medium. The rubric's "high" is wrong output or a broken main-path feature, but HEAD emits correct plans: the guard at :374 is present, correct, and I verified it selects the colind-matching block. Nothing is currently wrong for a user. This is a mutation-survival/regression-risk finding: an unpinned invariant whose removal WOULD be high (silently wrong collision on a block that can reach up to 55 chunks), but the defect is latent, not live. Medium is the honest rating for "correct code, zero test pinning it".

findings.title: planSurfaceEdit locked-tile refusals untested in both paint modes
findings.claim: Both 'tile N is not editable' refusals in planSurfaceEdit (link mode :175-177, isolate mode :209-211) can be deleted without failing any test — the Paint path's lock enforcement wiring is unpinned.
findings.evidence: PLANTS: removed the link-mode refusal (lines 175-177) → 22/22 pass; separately removed the isolate-mode refusal (lines 209-211) → 22/22 pass (classic-surface-plan.test.ts, the only consumer). The predicate itself (tileLockReason) IS tested (editable-tiles.test.ts caught my anim-range plant with 2 failures), but nothing proves the planner calls it. Failure scenario: regression drops the call → pencil paints an anim-overlay or appended tile, producing an edit the save path later errors on ('animated art slots are not editable in v1'), i.e. work the artist cannot save. Save-path defense means no silent corruption, hence medium not high.

findings.title: Commit-plan freeSlot allocation filter (reserved/anim/locked) untested
findings.claim: Deleting the `reserved.has(t) || animTiles.has(t) || !isEditableTile(t)` filter from the commit planner's freeSlot (classic-commit-plan.ts:299) leaves all 24 tests green — nothing proves a canvas commit refuses to allocate into object-reserved, animated, or non-editable tile slots.
findings.evidence: PLANT: rewrote the freeSlot loop body to `return t` unconditionally after the usage check → classic-commit-plan.test.ts 24/24 pass. Failure scenario: a commit allocates new art into an anim-overlay slot → art bound there animates in game; or into an appended/gap tile → save errors after the fact. Contrast: the surface-plan twin of this filter IS partially pinned — my double-booking plant (removed `taken.has(t)` at classic-surface-plan.ts:106) was CAUGHT by the 'slot double-booking (regression)' describe at classic-surface-plan.test.ts:421.

findings.title: blocks-exhausted and tiles-exhausted refusals have no core-level test
findings.claim: Removing the MAX_BLOCKS_TOTAL ceiling (`if (id >= MAX_BLOCKS_TOTAL) return null;` at :388) leaves all tests green; the 'blocks-exhausted' and 'tiles-exhausted' refusal kinds are exercised nowhere against the real planner.
findings.evidence: PLANT: deleted the ceiling check → 24/24 pass. grep across all tests: 'blocks-exhausted'/'tiles-exhausted' appear only in canvas-commit-model.test.ts:101-121, which formats UI messages from HAND-BUILT refusal objects (a mock of the planner's output, not the planner). chunks-exhausted, by contrast, is genuinely pinned (classic-commit-plan.test.ts:337 with expect.fail else-arm — I verified the pattern). Failure scenario: block id 0x400+ flows into the 10-bit chunk-cell field on save and is truncated/corrupted. Rare in practice (needs >1024 blocks), hence medium.
findings.fix: Two tests: a doc at MAX_BLOCKS_TOTAL blocks committing one new block shape → expect blocks-exhausted; a doc with zero free/reclaimable tile slots committing new art → expect tiles-exhausted with the reported counts.

findings.title: Both save self-check gates: byte-mismatch arm is dead code to the suite
findings.claim: The re-decode-and-compare halves of the two write-path self-checks (s1-io.ts emitCompressed :408 and s1-art-write.ts encodeS1ArtWriteBack :121) can be disabled (`if (false && ...)`) with every test still green — only the decoder-THROWS arm is ever exercised, though both modules' headers claim tests prove the gate fires.
findings.evidence: PLANT (s1-io): `if (!bytesEqual(dec, raw))` → `if (false as boolean && ...)` → s1-io.test.ts + classic-save.test.ts 34/34 pass. PLANT (s1-art-write): same disable at :121 → 8/8 pass. Cause: the injected broken encoders produce UNDECODABLE output (s1-io.test.ts:263 `brokenNemesis = () => new Uint8Array([0,0,0,0])`; s1-art-write.test.ts:104 truncates the stream), so nemesisDecompress throws and the catch arm (:412/:124) returns the same refusal. Failure scenario the untested arm exists for: a compressor bug that emits a VALID stream decoding to different bytes — precisely the silent-corruption case — would pass the gate and write wrong art into the disasm.
findings.fix: In each gate test, additionally inject a compressor that returns the real compression of MUTATED input (e.g. nemesisCompress of raw with one byte flipped) — decodes cleanly to wrong bytes — and assert the self-check refusal fires.

findings.title: performGuardedWrite (main-process fs half of guarded save) has zero tests
findings.claim: The fs-effecting half of the guarded save — unsafe-relPath throw, tmp+rename atomic write, orphan-tmp cleanup, and the partial-batch {written,newMtimes,failed,unwritten} contract — is exercised by no test, despite the header (:4-5) saying it was extracted 'so the whole cycle is unit-testable headlessly'.
findings.evidence: grep 'performGuardedWrite' across all *.test.* files: zero hits; its only caller is ipc-handlers.ts:53. src/main contains no test files at all (find). Renderer-side tests (classic-save.test.ts etc.) stub the write bridge with vi.fn handles. The pure decision table IS solid — my two save-guard plants were caught (4 and 1 failures) — but the code that turns a plan into disk writes, including the partial-batch reporting the renderer's error UI depends on, runs for the first time in production. Failure scenario: a regression in the partial-batch path (e.g. failed file omitted from `failed`) silently misreports which disasm files landed after a mid-batch fs error.
findings.fix: Add src/main/__tests__/guarded-write.test.ts using a tmpdir: happy path returns newMtimes matching fs.stat; conflict path writes nothing; an EACCES-forced failure mid-batch yields correct written/failed/unwritten and no leftover .tmp; '../escape' relPath throws before any stat.

findings.title: 32 test files pin .tsx behavior by regex over source text
findings.claim: 32 of 171 test files assert by readFileSync-ing .tsx source and matching text (e.g. classic-art-dock.test.ts:152 pins a literal `finally { ...clearAction(); }` shape; facet-modules 8 such blocks, facet-visibility 6, palette-grid-wiring 6, map-status-model 5) — these pass whenever the text survives, even if the behavior around it breaks.
findings.evidence: Static sweep (scratchpad/sweep.mjs) + `grep -rln readFileSync ... | xargs grep -l .tsx` = 32 files. The pattern is honest and self-documented (zoom-cap.test.ts header: 'pinned by source scan... must be checked by hand in the app') and is a structural consequence of the node-only suite (matches the known runtime-only-bugs constraint). Example vacuity: classic-art-dock.test.ts:143 `toMatch(/s\.pendingAction/)` passes if TileTab reads pendingAction into a dead variable. Not per-file negligence — a suite-architecture ceiling; these tests are worth keeping but must not be counted as behavioral coverage.
findings.fix: No per-file fix; the honest ledger is: treat source-scan blocks as tripwires, and route new .tsx-behavior guarantees through extracted pure modules (the codebase already does this well — zoom-cap, free-tile-slots, palette-grid-model are all extractions with real tests) or through the CDP-driven checks used elsewhere.

findings.title: Baseline suite is flaky: 2 facet-mount tests failed once, green on rerun
findings.claim: At the pinned commit the first full `npx vitest run` failed 2 tests ('s1ArtFacet mounts the pixel chrome › declares both a ToolDock and a ToolOptions' via dynamic import of s1-facets, plus one sibling) and passed 2914/2914 on two immediate re-runs — a nondeterministic failure mode that trains people to re-run red suites.
findings.evidence: Run 1: 'Test Files 2 failed | 263 passed, Tests 2 failed | 2912 passed'; runs 2 and 3 (same tree, no changes): all green (scratchpad/baseline.txt). The failing block dynamically imports '../facets/s1-facets' inside the test; symptom is consistent with a module-graph/timing race under parallel workers. I did not root-cause it.
findings.fix: Reproduce under `--sequence.shuffle` / repeated runs to bisect the import race; consider hoisting the dynamic import or isolating the facet-module tests into their own pool.
